Conditional correlation-based R2 (corR2) for a fitted rrGDM model

Source: R/corR2.R
cor_r2.Rd

Computes the conditional corR2 of a fitted rrGDM object: the squared Pearson correlation between the observed dissimilarities used to fit the model and the dissimilarities implied by the conditional latent coordinates (i.e., including sample-level errors and any other random effects), after applying the inverse link function.

Usage

cor_r2(object, message = FALSE)

Arguments

object

A fitted object of class rrGDM.

message

Logical. Should a message clarifying the interpretation of the corR2 be printed? Default is TRUE.

Value

A single numeric value: the conditional corR2, between 0 and 1.

Details

The corR2 is useful to assess how well the latent space captures the observed dissimilarities (e.g., to choose the number of latent dimensions k), but it is not a measure of the explanatory power of the predictors. Because the conditional coordinates include the sample-level errors, the corR2 can be high even if the predictors explain little. Like stress, it increases as k increases, so it is best used descriptively.

Examples

set.seed(2)
# simulate data
n <- 25 # sites
p <- 25 # species

env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,
            dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))

# fit model
fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
             formula = ~ temp + moist,
             family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done
#> 
#> ℹ optimisation
#> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 1670.1661
#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 

cor_r2(fit)
#> [1] 0.9549986
